newsitem.title: USA: FBI to ask again for help in Olympic bombing.
newsitem.headline: FBI to ask again for help in Olympic bombing.

text.p: The Federal Bureau of Investigation will make a new appeal to the public for information that could help its investigation of last year's bombing of Centennial Olympic Park, a spokesman said Wednesday.
FBI spokesman Jay Spadafore said the agency would make "a request for further assistance from the public" at a news conference scheduled for 1 p.m. EST Thursday.
He would not comment on a newspaper report that senior FBI officials told members of Congress to expect more bombings in Atlanta following three bomb attacks in seven months.

Spadafore told Reuters he could not confirm the report by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution that four members of Georgia's congressional delegation were told by FBI officials at a closed-door meeting in Washington last week that those responsible for the bombings would likely strike again.
Two people have died and more than 120 have been injured as a result of the three attacks.

Federal agents were investigating the bombings under the theory that bombs planted at an Atlanta abortion clinic in January and at a gay and lesbian nightclub last month were related, the article said.
Investigators also were agressively exploring the theory that those attacks were tied to the deadly Centennial Olympic Park bombing, which left two people dead and more than 100 injured last July.
The FBI believed Atlanta has been singled out as a target for bombings partly because of international exposure the city gained as host of the 1996 Olympics.

They also told Sen. Paul Coverdell, Representative Mac Collins and Representative Bob Barr, all Georgia Republicans, and Democratic Representative John Lewis that law enforcement officials were one of the primary targets in all three bombings.
The abortion clinic and nightclub attacks involved two devices, including so-called "sucker" bombs timed to explode after police and rescue workers had arrived on the scene.
The Centennial Olympic Park bomb exploded 10 minutes earlier than the time given police by an anonymous caller.
